chunks: From him, from Saad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubaid, from Ali ibn Hakam and Ali ibn Hasan ibn Nafe, from Harun ibn Kharja, who said:

Harun ibn Saad al-Ajali said to me: 'Ismail, to whom you were looking forward [with hope for his Imamate], has died. And Ja'far is an old man who will die tomorrow or the day after, so you will remain without an Imam.' I did not know what to say, so I informed Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) of his statement. He said: 'Far off, far off! Allah willed, by Allah, that this matter [of Imamate] will not be cut off until the night and day are cut off. When you see him, tell him: This is Musa ibn Ja'far who is growing up, and we will marry him, and a son will be born to him, and he will be a successor, if Allah wills.'

key_terms.إِسْمَاعِيلُ: Ismail ibn Ja'far, the previous Imam whose death caused concern.
key_terms.إِمَامٌ: Imam, the divinely appointed leader and successor of the Prophet.
key_terms.جَعْفَرٌ: Ja'far ibn Muhammad (al-Sadiq), the current Imam at the time of the narration.
key_terms.خَلِيفَةً: Successor/Caliph, referring to the one who will succeed Musa ibn Ja'far in the Imamate.
key_terms.مُوسَى بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ: Musa ibn Ja'far (al-Kadhim), the next Imam, son of Ja'far.

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq predict about the continuation of the Imamate after the death of Ismail ibn Ja'far?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* addresses the critical 'Ismailiyya' crisis, where followers feared the Imamate ended with the death of Ismail ibn Ja'far. Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) provided a definitive theological reassurance that the divine authority (al-Amr) is perpetual until the end of time, explicitly predicting the rise of Musa ibn Ja'far and his son to ensure continuity. This establishes the foundational Shia doctrine of the uninterrupted line of Imams despite political or familial uncertainties.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 22 - It is narrated from Saad bin Abdullah from Muhammad bin Isa bin Ubaid from Ali bin Hakam and Ali bin Hasan Nafe from Harun bin Kharja that he said:

Harun bin Saad Ajali said to me: Ismail, to whom you are inclined [and in whose Imamate you hope], has died. Ja’far [Imam Sadiq] is also aged and would pass away these days and you would remain without an Imam. I did not know what to reply. I mentioned this to Imam Sadiq (a.s). Imam (a.s) said: Never, by Allah! The Almighty Allah would never discontinue the matter of Imamate as long as the days and nights endure. When you meet him, tell him: This Musa bin Ja’far is growing up and we will get him married and he would get a son, who would be his Caliph and successor, if Allah wills.
